## Setup

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(lme4) # probably a bit too optimistic with the amount of data we have!
```

## Background

I ran coding queries on PPCHY and our finished files, looking for pronominal object / RP / RP-H following non-finite verbs in IP-MAT, IP-SUB, IP-INF and IP-PPL.

I also grabbed the ones with pronominal object / RP / RP-H preceding non-finite verbs, for a fuller picture. In these, I have excluded cases where the pronominal object precedes a finite auxiliary, as I'm assuming that these would not be informative.

### Summary of Variables

| Variable | Labels | Comments |
| -------- | ------ | -------- |
| `ClauseType` | `mat`, `sub`, `inf` | IP-MAT, IP-SUB, IP-INF |
| `WordOrder` | `ov`, `vo`, `badone` | "v" being the non-finite verb, "o" being a catch-all for pronominal object, RP, RP-H. `badone` is for cases where there is something relevant both preceding and following the non-finite verb. |
| `Element` | `rp`, `object`, `both` | `rp` includes both RP and RP-H (can make adjustments if this is not what we want). `both` flags cases where there's both a pronominal object and an RP/RP-H in the specified `WordOrder` position |
| `Genre` | | PPCHY ones need fixing, the ones from our parsed files should be ok. |
| `Corpus` | `ppchy`, `ourcorpus` | The files the data comes from. |
| `Text` |  | Whatever is printed in the ID labels |
| `Token` |  | Token label within the text, stripped off of ID label |

We'll want to add `Year` in as well, but the labelling in PPCHY is a bit tricky.

## Prepare Data

Load data, add variable names:

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
d1 <- read.delim("marjuqueries.ppchy.nodates.cod.ooo", header=F, sep=":")
d2 <- read.delim("marjuqueries.ourcorpus.nodates.cod.ooo", header=F, sep=":")

d <- rbind(d1, d2)
colnames(d) <- c("ClauseType", "WordOrder", "Element", "Genre", "Corpus", "Text", "Token")
head(d)
nrow(d)
```

Remove irrelevant instances with `z`:

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
data <- subset(d, ClauseType != "z" & WordOrder != "z" & Element != "z")

nrow(data)
```

Turn strings to factors, check:

```{r}
data <- mutate_if(data, is.character, as.factor)

summary(data)
```


## Descriptive Stats

The number of postverbal thingies in the different clause types:

```{r}
freq <- table(data$ClauseType, data$WordOrder)
freq
```

And percentages for each clause type:

```{r}
round(prop.table(freq, margin = 1) * 100, 3)
```

And a look at the different elements:

```{r}
table(data$ClauseType, data$WordOrder, data$Element)
```

Pulling out the VO tokens

```{r}
vo_data <- subset(data, WordOrder == "vo")

vo_data %>% add_count(Text) %>% arrange(desc(n)) %>% select(-c(WordOrder, Token, n)) %>% summary
# sorted by which text has the most of these, as the summary function only shows the first few instances 
```

How are these distributed?

```{r}
table(vo_data$ClauseType, vo_data$Genre)
```

Currently, all the "xxxgenre" ones are from PPCHY as the labels are not very consistent.
